question: The Widal test is the gold standard for diagnosing typhoid fever in children because it detects Salmonella Typhi antibodies reliably from the first week of illness.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is FALSE. The Widal test has multiple limitations: delayed positivity (week 2 onwards), false positives from malaria, typhoid vaccination, and prior infection, and poor specificity. Blood culture is the gold standard for typhoid diagnosis, with positivity highest in the first 2 weeks of illness. A positive Widal alone without clinical correlation leads to overdiagnosis and overtreatment.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. The Widal test is neither sensitive nor specific enough to be the gold standard. It turns positive only after 1–2 weeks (useless in the first week), cross-reacts with other Salmonella species and malaria, and prior vaccination or prior infection raises baseline titres. Blood culture (positive in ~60–80% in the first 2 weeks) is the gold standard. Bone marrow culture is most sensitive but rarely practical.
